title: Understanding Inter-Session Intentions via Complex Logical Reasoning

problem.claim: Product and attribute recommendations must account for intricate user intentions spanning multiple sessions and connected by logical operators.

gap.claim: Existing session-understanding research has not adequately addressed recommendations for such complex intentions.

contributions.claim: Introduces logical session complex query answering (LS-CQA) and formulates complex intention understanding as LS-CQA on an aggregated hypergraph of sessions, items, and attributes.
Introduces the Logical Session Graph Transformer (LSGT) to model interactions among items across sessions and their logical connections.
Analyzes LSGT expressiveness and proves permutation invariance of inputs for the logical operators.

stated_novelty.claim: The paper presents LS-CQA as a unique complex query-answering task with sessions represented as ordered hyperedges and introduces LSGT as a new model.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that LSGT achieves state-of-the-art results on three datasets.

narrative_sequence.summary: User intentions are important for recommendation, navigation, and query reformulation, but can span sessions and involve logical attribute requirements.
Existing session-understanding research does not adequately handle recommendations for these complex intentions.
The paper defines LS-CQA and represents the problem using an aggregated hypergraph of sessions, items, and attributes.
The paper introduces LSGT to capture cross-session item interactions and logical connections.
The paper analyzes expressiveness, proves permutation invariance for logical-operator inputs, and reports state-of-the-art results on three datasets.

source_observation.claim: The task represents sessions as ordered hyperedges and aggregates sessions, items, and attributes into a hypergraph.

interpretation.claim: Structured representations can make cross-session relationships and logical constraints explicit.

application.claim: For multi-session recommendation or intent modeling, consider representations that preserve session structure and logical relations.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish that this representation is preferable for domains without multi-session or logical intent structure.

unknowns: The abstract does not identify the three datasets, baselines, metrics, or quantitative results.
The abstract does not describe the model architecture, training procedure, or computational requirements in detail.
The abstract does not provide examples of the expressiveness analysis or the permutation-invariance proof.
